rationale: The analysis correctly identifies the downstream rate-limit reduction (E4) as the initiating cause, with 429-triggered retry/backoff (E5) as the proximate latency mechanism, and explicitly demonstrates via E6 that latency elevation partitions by 429 status rather than cache outcome. It correctly reclassifies the cache hit-rate decline as a downstream effect of the retry cache-bypass header (E7), supported by the healthy cache service report (E3), and closes the loop with the rate-limit restoration and recovery (E8). All four required findings are present and the forbidden claim (cache degradation as cause) is explicitly and repeatedly rejected (C8, R7, R9), including a counterfactual (CF1) that states what evidence would be needed to overturn this. All claims and relationships cite only supplied evidence IDs with no outside-evidence use. Uncertainty is well-calibrated: despite high per-claim confidence, the analysis surfaces genuine residual unknowns (retry-timing decomposition, root cause of the rate-limit change, recurrence risk) and pairs each with a concrete discriminating observation, consistent with the case's low stated uncertainty. Actions are prioritized correctly, leading with restoring/governing the rate limit (the demonstrated controlling lever) and following with defense-in-depth measures (client-side throttling, retry tuning, removing the misleading cache-bypass artifact, better alerting) without weakening any protective control or exceeding the evidence. No secondary flags are warranted.
